message.content:
This is an electrical connector for a voltage of 1,000 V or less, so it falls in heading 8536. The relevant subheadings are 8536.69 (plugs and sockets) and 8536.90 (other apparatus). A 5-pin XLR plug that connects to a cable would be classified in 8536.69, not 8536.70 (fiber optic) or 8536.50 (switches).

For 8536.69, the subheadings are 8536.69.10 (for coaxial cable), 8536.69.20 (for printed circuits), and 8536.69.40 (other, for a voltage not exceeding 250 V, from the older schedule), with 8536.69.80 and 8536.69.90 as other residual lines. The current HTSUS has 8536.69.40 (Other: Plugs and sockets, for a voltage not exceeding 250 V) and 8536.69.80 (other). I recall that CBP rulings on XLR connectors for audio headsets (e.g., Zulu 3) place them in 8536.69.40 (the actual 10-digit number there is 8536.69.4000).

I am working from memory of the tariff schedule structure, so I'm not certain of the exact ten-digit statistical suffix. I chose 8536.69.40 over the "other" lines because I recall it as the line CBP uses for audio plug-and-socket connectors, and the text suggests ordinary low-voltage use.

{"hts_code": "8536.69.4000", "reason": "A 5-pin XLR plug connector for audio and power signals on a headset cable is an electrical plug/socket for a voltage not exceeding 1,000 V (heading 8536), classified under 8536.69 as 'other plugs and sockets'."}
